name: Felix Ohswald
profile: Austrian mathematician-turned-founder who co-founded GoStudent with Gregor Müller in 2016, building a one-to-one online tutoring platform that became Europe's first edtech unicorn (valued ~$3.5B in 2022). After a post-boom restructuring, GoStudent reported full-year operational profitability in 2025.
interesting_fact: Studied maths in Vienna and at Cambridge (BA Hons 2014), then a master's in quantitative finance at ETH Zurich, before quitting a finance path to start GoStudent.
deep_cut_fact: GoStudent began in 2015 when Ohswald, then 20 and at ETH Zurich, ran an online group answering schoolchildren's homework questions after helping his younger brother's friends with their schoolwork.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (ASU+GSV, 4GameChangers). Best route is the GoStudent press team.

name: Yoni Cheifetz
current_role: Partner, Lightspeed Venture Partners (heads Israel investment team); co-founder of Earnix
profile: Israeli software entrepreneur who co-founded insurance/banking pricing-analytics firm Earnix in 2001 with Sammy Krikler (valued ~$1B after Insight Partners' 2021 investment). Also co-founded or chaired Demantra (sold to Oracle), Agentics and Traiana; since 2006 he has led Lightspeed's Israel investing across AI, enterprise, fintech, climate and deep tech.
interesting_fact: A serial founder of nearly a dozen software companies before VC, including Demantra (acquired by Oracle), Agentics (acquired by Mercado) and Traiana (acquired by ICAP).
deep_cut_fact: Holds an MSc in applied mathematics and computer science from the Weizmann Institute, ran product management at ClickSoftware, and unwinds by kayaking and rowing: 'Somehow that makes me a better, or at least calmer, person.'
notes: Also listed as Jonathan Cheifetz in some filings. Says he tries to meet as many entrepreneurs as possible. Work email is the 'Get in Touch' link on his Lightspeed bio.

name: Omri Cohen
profile: Israeli engineer who co-founded Yotpo with Tomer Tagrin around 2011 after they met studying at Tel Aviv University. Yotpo grew into an e-commerce retention platform (reviews, loyalty, SMS) used by Shopify brands and reached a $1.4B valuation in 2021; Cohen remains co-founder and COO as the company refocuses on reviews, loyalty and AI.
interesting_fact: Tagrin has told Forbes that Cohen was 'the smart kid sitting in the front row taking notes' who turned around and told him to shut up so he could learn; the two have been best friends and co-founders ever since.
deep_cut_fact: Before Yotpo, Cohen worked on the ASIC team at Essence Security developing a future wireless MAC protocol, and earlier as a software engineer on a radio software team.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Tomer Tagrin; Yotpo cut ~200 jobs in Aug 2025 in a refocus. 'Omri Cohen' is a very common Israeli name; confirm via Yotpo. Deep-cut source is a secondary profile (Money Inc.).

name: Guilherme Nosralla
profile: Brazilian growth/marketing executive who co-founded Merama in 2020, a Latin American e-commerce group that takes majority stakes in leading online consumer brands and scales them across marketplaces. Merama became a unicorn about a year after founding, valued at ~$1.2B after a $60M Series B extension led by Advent and SoftBank in Dec 2021.
interesting_fact: Merama hit a US$1.2B valuation roughly one year after launch, one of the fastest unicorn runs in Latin America; the round also funded Merama Labs, an in-house unit for building new businesses.
notes: Low public profile; founding-team lists vary (Sujay Tyle is CEO; Renato Andrade, Felipe Delgado, Olivier Scialom also cited). A Web Summit Rio 2025 speaker page (now 404) said he was previously Growth Strategy Director at mobile-game maker Wildlife Studios; unverified. No published press email found; reach via Merama website/LinkedIn.

name: Theodore Feldman
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Medical Officer, Rightway (New York)
profile: Dr. Ted Feldman is a Miami cardiologist who co-founded Rightway in 2017 with his son, CEO Jordan Feldman, to give employees physician-backed help navigating healthcare. Rightway has since become a transparent pharmacy-benefits (PBM) alternative valued at over $1B, and was reported in Sept 2026 to be eyeing an IPO after new funding.
interesting_fact: Rightway's founding story is a family one: Jordan Feldman grew up with a cardiologist father at his side and saw how transformative expert clinical guidance could be, so the two set out to give every member that access.
deep_cut_fact: A Harvard College and Albert Einstein College of Medicine graduate, he trained in cardiology at the University of Miami/Jackson Memorial and has served as medical director of the South Miami Heart Center and Baptist Health South Florida's Center for Healthy Living.
notes: Practising physician with low media profile; son Jordan Feldman (CEO) is the public face. Rightway's about page says media inquiries go to info@rightwayhealthcare.com; press page also lists press@. Deep-cut bio is from a CME faculty page (Miami cardiologist Theodore Feldman) - matches but not explicitly linked to Rightway there.

name: Justin Bajko
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer, Expel (since Nov 2025)
profile: Security-operations veteran who co-founded managed detection and response (MDR) firm Expel in 2016 with fellow Mandiant alumni Dave Merkel and Yanek Korff; Expel reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. Long its VP of Strategy and Business Development, he became Chief Strategy Officer in Nov 2025, overseeing corporate and product strategy including AI in the SOC.
interesting_fact: Before Expel he ran Mandiant's Managed Defense, one of the industry's first MDR services, and then built FireEye's global SOCs as senior director of global service delivery; earlier he worked at Symantec.
deep_cut_fact: Expel's own profile calls him a University of Tennessee football fan and 'video game connoisseur'; he has compared bloated security platforms to cable TV, where 'you have to buy 100 channels just to access the specific one you want.'
notes: Publicly invites outreach in his CSO announcement ('Reach out. I'd love to chat.'). Route via Expel comms.

name: Jeff Zheng
current_role: Founder and CEO, NewsBreak (Particle Media), Mountain View, CA
profile: Search and recommendation engineer who led Yahoo Labs in Beijing, then left in 2011 to launch Chinese news app Yidian Zixun before founding NewsBreak in Silicon Valley in 2015. NewsBreak became one of the most-downloaded local-news apps in the US, raising $115M in 2021 at a $1B+ valuation; he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Former Microsoft AI and Bing chief Harry Shum became NewsBreak's board chairman in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: At Yahoo he headed Yahoo Labs Beijing, overseeing algorithm work across search, media, advertising and mobile, before leaving to build Yidian Zixun, the main rival to ByteDance's Toutiao.
notes: No published press email found (search budget ran out before confirming). Company has faced press scrutiny (2024 Reuters report on AI-generated stories and Chinese origins) - tread carefully. Approach via NewsBreak corporate site/LinkedIn.

name: Francesco Simoneschi
profile: Italian entrepreneur who co-founded TrueLayer in London in 2016 with Luca Martinetti to build open-banking payment infrastructure. Its Pay by Bank network is live in 22 countries with 30M+ users and clients like Ryanair and Just Eat; the company passed a $1B valuation in 2021 and recently took investment from Italy's CDP Venture Capital.
interesting_fact: TrueLayer pitches itself as homegrown European payment rails that bypass US card networks; Simoneschi: 'Europe deserves payment infrastructure built in Europe.'
deep_cut_fact: About a quarter of TrueLayer's workforce (around 70 people) is in Italy, with Milan as a core engineering hub; Simoneschi called Italy's CDP backing personally meaningful, a 'homecoming' for a company founded by two Italians.
notes: Search budget ran out; personal background (education, pre-TrueLayer jobs) not verified. Route via TrueLayer press.

name: Róbert Wessman
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Alvotech (Nasdaq/Nasdaq Iceland: ALVO)
profile: Icelandic pharma entrepreneur who turned generic-drug maker Delta into global player Actavis as CEO (1999-2008), then built Alvogen and founded Reykjavik-based biosimilar developer Alvotech in 2013. Alvotech listed in 2022; Wessman is now Executive Chairman, with Lisa Graver as CEO.
interesting_fact: A former competitive cyclist, he owns a vineyard in Saint-Cernin in southwest France and has launched wine labels with singer Norah Jones and with Kaleo frontman Jökull Júlíusson.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating in business from the University of Iceland in 1993 he spent seven years at shipping firm Samskip, rising to run its German operations, while also teaching mathematics part-time at the University of Iceland.
notes: Also linked to Alvogen and Lotus Pharmaceutical (Taiwan) via his investment vehicle Aztiq. Wikipedia infobox still lists him as CEO but Alvotech's site shows him as Executive Chairman. Avoid Actavis-era disputes.

name: Jacob Rubens
current_role: Founding team member, Tessera Therapeutics (Flagship Pioneering company); current title not verified
profile: Scientist (Ph.D.) on the founding team of Tessera Therapeutics with Noubar Afeyan and Geoffrey von Maltzahn at Flagship Pioneering. Tessera develops 'Gene Writing' genetic medicines, has a lead in vivo gene-editing program for AATD (TSRA-196) partnered with Regeneron, and has been valued at over $1B.
interesting_fact: Tessera's lead program TSRA-196 reached the clinic and is co-developed with Regeneron; the company also won up to $41.3M from ARPA-H to advance in vivo CAR-T therapies.
notes: Listed under 'Founding Team' on Tessera's leadership page. Believed to be a Flagship Pioneering origination partner, but Flagship's bio page was blocked (403) and search budget ran out, so current role and background are unverified. Tessera CEO since July 2026 is Joseph Romanelli.

name: Eyal Chameides
current_role: Co-founder and director, Tripledot Holdings (Tripledot Studios, London)
profile: Australian-born co-founder of Tripledot Studios, the London mobile casual-games publisher founded in 2017 and valued above $1B in 2021. Companies House shows him as a director of Tripledot Studios Ltd from 2018-2022 and an active director of parent Tripledot Holdings since Aug 2022. Wider background not verified in this pass.
interesting_fact: Although Tripledot is a London studio, UK Companies House records list Chameides' nationality as Australian.
notes: Web-search budget was exhausted before this person; role confirmed only via Companies House. Tripledot's site names no founders and gives no press email. Needs follow-up for background and press route.

name: Rujul Zaparde
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Zip (procurement software, San Francisco)
profile: Two-time YC founder who co-founded Zip in 2020 with Lu Cheng and Felix Meng to fix slow enterprise purchasing with an AI 'intake-to-pay' procurement platform. Zip raised $190M at a $2.2B valuation and says its agentic platform processed $355B in spend in 2025; he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: His first company, FlightCar (YC Winter 2013), was pitched as 'the Airbnb of car rentals at airports', letting travellers rent out their parked cars; it operated at 12 US airports with backers including Brian Chesky.
deep_cut_fact: Between FlightCar and Zip he worked at Y Combinator as a Visiting Partner.
notes: Media-friendly (YC talks with Dalton Caldwell on enterprise sales). Route via press@ziphq.com.
